text:
alex: quick check — onboarding weights for gau-xxl are uploaded to s3://redwood-models/gau-xxl/v1/weights.tgz (43.2GB). I untarred locally, looks like standard hf format but model.bin is sharded.
maria: ok thanks. can you confirm tokenizer files too? last time we had an extra <|mask|> token that shifted ids.
alex: tokenizer.json and merges present. vocab_size=50288. there is a special token <pad_extra> at id 50287, not in our usual vocab. wondering if we should remap or patch.
jin: +1 on checking remap. that extra token breaks our padding math for some batch code paths. small fix in tokenizers/patch_vocab.py should handle.
sam: FYI the config claims max_position_embeddings: 131072 — that'll be rough on 40GB GPUs if we allow full length in serving.
alex: yeah discovered that when running a quick dry-run. KV cache memory is ~ (hidden_size/2 * seq_len * 2) per layer in our current runtime because of key+value buffers + attention workspace.
jin: rough estimate: for gau-xxl with hidden 6144, 70 layers, seq=65536, batch=1, kv v2 -> OOM on a40/40GB. we should cap default max_seq_len for hosted to 65536 and for dedicated to configurable by instance type.
maria: is kv format v2 required? I saw two formats in the weights manifest.
alex: weights manifest lists "kv_cache_format": "v2" for optimized fastpath. v2 uses fused buffers that double peak mem during generation in our implementation. v1 is more conservative but slower.
sam: suggestion: add validator in onboarding that rejects max_seq_len > 65536 for v2 on <=40GB instances and autocorrect to v1 or lower max_seq_len with a warning.
jin: agreed. also add unit test to simulate chunked KV allocation.
alex: here's the config snippet I tested locally:
```yaml
model:
  name: gau-xxl
  weights_path: s3://redwood-models/gau-xxl/v1/
  max_seq_len: 131072
  kv_cache_format: v2
  quant: q4_0
```
alex: command I used for mem estimate:
```
./tools/mem-estimate --model gau-xxl --seq 65536 --batch 1 --kv v2 --layers 70 --hidden 6144
```
qa-bot: mem-estimate result: estimated_runtime_mem=58.3GB peak_total=62.1GB (exceeds 40GB)
deploy-bot: rollouts shouldn't allow this config on hosted tier :robot_face:
maria: ok I'll open a PR to add onboarding validation + token remap for the extra pad token. will also add an advisory note for customers about kv v2 behavior on smaller instances.
sam: pinging infra: if we keep v2 we should add an autoswap fallback to v1 when detect OOM on cold start. @jin can you file a follow-up for runtime fallback?
jin: will do. marking as blocker for onboarding until validator is merged.
alex: PR is here: https://github.com/redwood-inference/models/pull/482 (draft) — includes patch_vocab and onboarding validator tests. requesting review from @maria and @jin :eyes:
maria: taking a look today.
sam: small nit — also ensure tokenizer remap preserves existing token ids for old checkpoints. we don't want subtle drift in saved embeddings.
alex: good call. I'll add mapping test that loads an old embedding matrix and compares.
jin: once validator merged, let's run full smoke onboarding on a1-large and a1-xlarge to verify memory/latency profile.
maria: timeline? we prefer this in staging by EOD Friday.
alex: aiming for Thursday PR update, Friday staging run.
sam: thanks all. if anyone hits weird OOM traces, paste logs here and we can triage.
alex: will post logs if any. thanks :thumbsup:
